content:

questions.answer: I was born and grew up in Hanoi, which is located in the North of Vietnam. It is a huge bustling city known for its old streets and local food.
questions.example: I live there with my family, and we often visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the Old Quarter on weekends.
questions.q: Can you describe your hometown? What is it known for?
questions.reason: It has breathtaking, picturesque landmarks symbolizing the beauty of the city, along with a long history.

questions.answer: What I like most about living in my hometown is the people and the diverse, flavorful cuisine.
questions.example: Whenever I eat pho or bun cha with my friends at small street stalls, I feel happy and comfortable.
questions.q: What do you like most about living in your hometown?
questions.reason: People here are very kind, helpful, friendly, and hospitable, and there are lots of delicious dishes to enjoy.

questions.answer: Yes, I dislike the heavy traffic and air pollution, so I wish to improve public transport.
questions.example: During rush hour on weekdays, it takes me 45 minutes by motorbike to get to school because of traffic congestion.
questions.q: Is there anything you dislike or wish to improve about your hometown?
questions.reason: Living in a big city brings higher living expenses and noise or air pollution, which makes people feel stressed and exhausted.

title: Part 3 - Topic 1: Methods to Break Bad Habits
content:
Topic: Effective methods to break bad habits
Suggestions:
- Practicing strong self-discipline
- Replacing bad habits with healthy alternatives
- Seeking advice and emotional support from family and friends
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. Do you think it is easy or difficult for young people to change their bad habits? Why?
2. What is the most common negative habit among teenagers today?
3. How can parents and teachers assist young people in overcoming negative habits?

hint.coreTopic: effective ways to break bad habits

followUps.answer: I think it is quite difficult for young people to change their bad habits.
followUps.example: For example, a student knows staying up late gaming is bad, but still finds it hard to turn off the computer at 10 PM.
followUps.formula: Do you think ...? -> I think it is difficult... (Reason + Example)
followUps.q: Do you think it is easy or difficult for young people to change their bad habits? Why?
followUps.reason: Many teenagers lack proper guidance and self-control, and bad habits often give instant fun while healthy habits take time to show results.

followUps.answer: There are some common bad habits among teenagers today, and the biggest one is spending too much time on smartphones.
followUps.example: For instance, many teens watch social media videos for three or four hours every evening instead of exercising or talking with family.
followUps.q: What is the most common negative habit among teenagers today?
followUps.reason: Excessive screen time can affect physical health, reduce sleep, and lower study focus.

followUps.answer: I think parents and schools should work closely together to guide, listen, and support young people instead of just scolding them.
followUps.example: For example, schools can organize afternoon sports clubs so students spend less time playing video games at home.
followUps.q: How can parents and teachers assist young people in overcoming negative habits?
followUps.reason: They can help teens set realistic goals, offer healthy school clubs, and limit phone use during study hours.

mindmapPoints.expand: This is because setting clear rules, like creating a daily timetable, prevents us from wasting hours on lazy behaviors.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it is good for personal success and keeps our life organized.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Practicing strong self-discipline helps people control their daily actions and stop bad habits.

mindmapPoints.cue: Replacing bad habits with healthy alternatives
mindmapPoints.expand: For example, instead of eating fast food or scrolling on a phone at night, people can go jogging or read a book to relieve stress.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is beneficial to both physical health and mental health.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Replacing a bad habit with a good activity helps people change naturally without feeling bored.

mindmapPoints.cue: Seeking advice and emotional support from family and friends
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because loved ones can remind us politely, encourage us on hard days, and join healthy routines with us.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has positive effects on our confidence and long-term results.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Asking family and friends for support helps people stay motivated when changing habits.

hint.ownIdea: I think that 3 ideas are comprehensive. I cannot think of other ideas.

title: Part 3 - Topic 2: Benefits of Participating in Team Sports
content:
Topic: The far-reaching benefits of playing team sports
Suggestions:
- Enhancing cardiovascular health and physical endurance
- Learning strategic collaboration and communication under pressure
- Building enduring camaraderie and social friendships
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. Why do some people prefer individual athletic activities over group sports?
2. What lessons from team sports can be applied to professional workplace environments?
3. How can schools encourage students who are not naturally athletic to take part in team games?

hint.coreTopic: the benefits of playing team sports

followUps.answer: This is mainly because individual sports offer more freedom over your schedule and a peaceful time alone.
followUps.example: For example, an office worker can run in the park for 30 minutes at 6 AM alone without booking a football field.
followUps.q: Why do some people prefer individual athletic activities over group sports?
followUps.reason: Busy people can go jogging or swimming whenever they are free without waiting for ten other teammates.

followUps.answer: There are some valuable lessons from team sports for the workplace, such as teamwork, responsibility, and staying calm under pressure.
followUps.example: For instance, a team member who learned to cooperate in university volleyball often works smoothly with coworkers on tight deadlines.
followUps.q: What lessons from team sports can be applied to professional workplace environments?
followUps.reason: Just like on the sports field, company workers must support colleagues, share goals, and accept feedback to finish projects well.

followUps.answer: I think schools should offer fun, beginner-friendly games and upgrade sports facilities instead of focusing only on winning prizes.
followUps.example: For example, schools can hold friendly badminton or relay games every Friday where every class participates for fun.
followUps.formula: How ...? -> Support solution (Schools upgrade facilities & clubs)
followUps.q: How can schools encourage students who are not naturally athletic to take part in team games?
followUps.reason: When games are relaxed and inclusive, shy students feel comfortable joining to make friends and stay active rather than worrying about scores.

mindmapPoints.cue: Enhancing cardiovascular health and physical endurance
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because running and moving actively in games like football or basketball helps us strengthen our immune system and feel more energetic.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it is good for our physical health and reduces stress after work or study.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Playing team sports helps people keep fit, strengthen their heart, and stay healthy.

mindmapPoints.cue: Learning strategic collaboration and communication under pressure
mindmapPoints.expand: For example, players must pass the ball, listen to teammates, and make quick decisions together to win a match.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is beneficial to their teamwork and problem-solving abilities.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Playing in a team helps people improve teamwork and communication skills.

mindmapPoints.cue: Building enduring camaraderie and social friendships
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because sports clubs let us meet like-minded people who share the same hobby and build a strong sense of belonging.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has positive effects on our social network and mental health.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Joining team sports brings people together and builds strong friendships.

title: Part 2 - Situation 3: Preparing for a Workplace Presentation
content:
Situation: You are preparing for an important upcoming project presentation at your workplace. You want to choose the most effective rehearsal method. There are three options:
- Practicing speaking in front of a mirror (luyện tập nói trước gương)
- Recording your speech and listening back to self-correct (thu âm và nghe lại để tự sửa)
- Rehearsing in front of a small group of colleagues for direct feedback (tập dượt trước một nhóm đồng nghiệp để nhận phản hồi)
Which option do you think is the best choice and why?

chosen.khen1Text: because it is easy to arrange with a few coworkers at the office without requiring any complicated equipment or preparation.

khen2ARE.answer: Rehearsing in front of colleagues helps me solve presentation problems early and adapt well to the workplace environment.
khen2ARE.example: For example, I can gather three teammates in a meeting room for twenty minutes after lunch, present my project slides, and ask them which parts need clearer examples.
khen2ARE.reason: Face-to-face interaction lets my colleagues point out unclear ideas or nervous body language right away, so I can fix weak points before the real presentation.

chosen.khen3Text: a safe and practical environment to gain real presentation experience, build confidence, and get ready for success at work.
chosen.option: Rehearsing in front of a small group of colleagues for direct feedback

rejected.option: Practicing speaking in front of a mirror
rejected.reason: talking to myself in front of a mirror feels awkward and cannot tell me whether my project ideas are clear or persuasive to real listeners.

rejected.option: Recording your speech and listening back to self-correct
rejected.reason: listening only to a voice recording misses my eye contact and posture, and I might still fail to notice my own mistakes without another person's feedback.

reusedVocab: adjust and adapt to the social environment

title: Part 3 - Topic 3: Negative Effects of Technology on Learning Habits
content:
Topic: The detrimental effects of modern digital technology on students' learning habits
Suggestions:
- Information overload and superficial reading
- Heavy reliance on search engines and automated tools
- Deteriorating critical thinking and independent reasoning
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. How does multitasking with smartphones during study hours affect students' memory retention?
2. What practical habits can learners adopt to avoid digital distractions while studying?
3. Do you think conventional handwritten notes are more effective for deep learning than typing on laptops?

hint.coreTopic: the negative effects of digital technology on students' learning

followUps.answer: Checking a smartphone while studying seriously weakens memory and makes learning much slower.
followUps.example: For example, a student who replies to chat messages while reading English vocabulary often forgets most of the words the next day.
followUps.q: How does multitasking with smartphones during study hours affect students' memory retention?
followUps.reason: Every time a message notification pops up, the student's brain loses focus and cannot store new knowledge deeply.

followUps.answer: There are some simple habits learners can use, such as turning off notifications and creating a clear daily study timetable.
followUps.example: For instance, using a paper notebook and leaving the phone on silent mode in a schoolbag helps students stay focused during homework.
followUps.formula: What ...? -> There are some... + Self-discipline solution
followUps.q: What practical habits can learners adopt to avoid digital distractions while studying?
followUps.reason: Putting the phone in another room for 45 minutes helps students build good self-discipline and finish urgent assignments faster.

followUps.answer: Yes, I think writing notes by hand is often better for deep learning than typing on a laptop.
followUps.example: For example, students who write mindmaps on paper during lectures usually remember lessons better before exams than those who type every word.
followUps.formula: Do you think ...? -> Yes, I think... (Reason + Example)
followUps.q: Do you think conventional handwritten notes are more effective for deep learning than typing on laptops?
followUps.reason: Handwriting is slower, so students must listen carefully and summarize key ideas in their own words, which allows their brain to exercise.

mindmapPoints.expand: This is because scrolling through endless online posts and notifications makes it hard to focus on one long textbook.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it has a negative effect on students' concentration and memory.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Students can face too much information and read quickly without deep understanding.

mindmapPoints.cue: Heavy reliance on search engines and automated tools
mindmapPoints.expand: For example, many learners just copy answers from the internet for homework instead of reading and solving exercises by themselves.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is harmful to their real learning progress and honest study habits.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Students can depend too much on search engines and AI tools for answers.

mindmapPoints.cue: Deteriorating critical thinking and independent reasoning
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because when devices do all the thinking, learners do not allow their brain to exercise or analyze ideas carefully.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has negative effects on their academic skills and future job readiness.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Using technology too much can weaken students' independent thinking and problem-solving skills.

hint.ownIdea: I think that 3 ideas are comprehensive. I cannot think of other ideas.

content:

questions.answer: Sometimes I pay attention to advertisements on social media, especially when I need to buy something new.
questions.example: When scrolling Facebook in the evening, I sometimes stop to watch short ads for English books or sports shoes.
questions.q: Do you often pay attention to advertisements on TV or social media?
questions.reason: Watching ads gives me useful information about new products and discounts, though too many ads can be annoying when I want to relax.

questions.answer: The most memorable advertisement I have seen is a Tet holiday commercial for a tea brand.
questions.example: It showed a young worker travelling home to have dinner with his parents on New Year's Eve, and I watched it with my family on TV.
questions.q: What is the most impressive or memorable advertisement you have ever seen, and why?
questions.reason: It had soft, gentle music and conveyed a touching message about family reunion, which made me feel warm and nostalgic.

questions.answer: No, I usually do not buy products right after watching an advertisement.
questions.example: Before buying a new backpack online, I always read real customer reviews first instead of trusting the video ad.

questions.reason: Ads often tempt buyers to waste money on cheap items that look nothing like the advertised photos, so I prefer to stay on the safe side, think things through calmly, and choose items that fit comfortably within my budget.

title: Part 3 - Topic 4: Disadvantages of Living in an Apartment
content:
Topic: Disadvantages of living in an apartment
Suggestions:
- Limited living space
- Pet restrictions
- Neighbor issues and noise
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. Do people around you prefer living in private houses or apartments? Why?
2. What challenges do families with pets or young children face in apartment buildings?
3. How can residents maintain good relationships with their neighbors in an apartment?

hint.coreTopic: the disadvantages of living in an apartment

followUps.answer: Many young people around me prefer apartments, while older families still prefer private houses.
followUps.example: For example, young office couples often choose a two-bedroom apartment near their workplace, while parents with two kids prefer a house with a small yard.
followUps.q: Do people around you prefer living in private houses or apartments? Why?
followUps.reason: Apartments are convenient for busy people with good security and shared facilities, whereas private houses give more space, privacy, and long-term value.

followUps.answer: There are some common challenges for them, such as noise complaints and a lack of safe play areas.
followUps.example: For instance, parents must always watch their kids on high balconies and take dogs downstairs in the elevator several times a day.
followUps.q: What challenges do families with pets or young children face in apartment buildings?
followUps.reason: Young children love running and pets may bark, which easily annoys downstairs neighbors, and high balconies can also be unsafe.

followUps.answer: I think residents should respect shared rules, keep noise low at night, and communicate politely with neighbors.
followUps.example: For example, if a family plans to repair their room or hold a small birthday party, telling next-door neighbors in advance keeps everyone happy.
followUps.q: How can residents maintain good relationships with their neighbors in an apartment?
followUps.reason: Being friendly in the elevator, keeping common hallways clean, and cleaning up after pets builds trust and avoids unnecessary trouble.

mindmapPoints.expand: This is because most apartments do not have a private yard or garden for children to play or for families to plant trees.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it can feel uncomfortable for big families who need more room.
mindmapPoints.sentence: The living space in an apartment is quite small and limited.

mindmapPoints.expand: For example, many buildings ban dogs and cats, or owners cannot find enough open space for their pets to run safely.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is inconvenient for animal lovers who want warm companionship at home.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Residents often face strict rules against keeping pets in apartment buildings.

mindmapPoints.expand: This is because shared walls and floors let loud music, footsteps, or crying children disturb your personal privacy and peace.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has negative effects on people's rest and mental health.
mindmapPoints.sentence: People living in apartments can easily suffer from noise and neighbor problems.

hint.ownIdea: I think that 3 ideas are comprehensive. I cannot think of other ideas.

title: Topic 7: Breakfast Habits & Nutrition
content:
1. What do you usually have for breakfast?
2. Do you prefer eating breakfast at home or eating out? Why?
3. How important is breakfast to your health and daily energy?

questions.answer: I usually have something simple and quick like bread with eggs, sticky rice, or a bowl of pho.
questions.example: On weekday mornings around 7 a.m., I often eat two boiled eggs, bread, and drink a glass of milk before leaving home.
questions.q: What do you usually have for breakfast?
questions.reason: These dishes are tasty, affordable, and fast and convenient for busy people in modern-day society.

questions.answer: I prefer eating breakfast at home with my family whenever I have time.
questions.example: Every morning, my mom cooks noodle soup or fried rice at home, and we eat together in the kitchen.
questions.q: Do you prefer eating breakfast at home or eating out? Why?
questions.reason: Home-cooked food is cleaner, healthier, and fits comfortably within my budget, and it also helps strengthen bonds within my family.

questions.answer: Breakfast plays an essential role in my physical health and daily energy.
questions.example: Whenever I skip breakfast on busy days, I feel tired and cannot concentrate in my morning classes.
questions.q: How important is breakfast to your health and daily energy?
questions.reason: Eating a good breakfast helps me feel more energetic, allows my brain to focus better at school or work, and prevents stomach problems.

content:
1. Do you use your mobile phone frequently in your daily life?
2. What purposes do you mostly use your mobile phone for?

questions.answer: Yes, I use my mobile phone every day because it is fast and convenient for busy people in modern-day society.
questions.example: I spend about two to three hours a day on my phone, mostly in the morning and evening.
questions.q: Do you use your mobile phone frequently in your daily life?
questions.reason: It helps me keep in touch with my family and friends, check study schedules, and make the most of new technology to improve productivity.

questions.answer: I mostly use my phone for studying English, chatting with friends, and relaxing with music or videos.
questions.example: Every evening, I use a dictionary app to learn new vocabulary and listen to soft music on Spotify.
questions.q: What purposes do you mostly use your mobile phone for?
questions.reason: It helps me broaden my knowledge easily and recharge my batteries when I feel stressed after school.

questions.answer: Yes, I think many people today rely too much on their phones, especially young people.
questions.example: Even at family dinners or coffee shops with friends, many people keep looking at their phone screens instead of talking.
questions.q: Do you think people today rely too much on their mobile phones?
questions.reason: Using phones too much reduces face-to-face interaction, hurts our eyes, and widens the generation gap when family members do not talk to each other.

title: Part 3 - Topic 5: Volunteering and Communication Skills
content:
Topic: Participating in volunteer work and personal development
Suggestions:
- Improving interpersonal and communication skills
- Gaining practical experience and teamwork abilities
- Contributing positively to the local community
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. What aspects of volunteering help improve your personal communication skills?
2. What difficulties do people often encounter when doing volunteer work, and what are the solutions?
3. How can schools and organizations encourage more young people to volunteer?

hint.coreTopic: participating in volunteer work and personal development

followUps.answer: There are some parts of volunteering that improve communication skills, such as talking with strangers, working in teams, and listening to people in need.
followUps.example: For example, when joining a blood donation event, volunteers explain the steps to visitors politely and work closely with doctors.
followUps.formula: What -> There are some [Ns], such as...
followUps.q: What aspects of volunteering help improve your personal communication skills?
followUps.reason: This is because volunteers must share ideas clearly and build a strong sense of belonging through face-to-face interaction.

followUps.answer: There are some common difficulties, such as lack of free time, low budgets, and feeling tired after hard work.
followUps.example: For instance, university clubs can plan weekend clean-up trips and give free lunch boxes to student volunteers.
followUps.formula: What -> There are some [Ns], such as... + Support solution
followUps.q: What difficulties do people often encounter when doing volunteer work, and what are the solutions?
followUps.reason: To solve this problem, volunteers should manage their schedule well, while organizations should provide clear training and financial support for travel and meals.

followUps.answer: I think schools and organizations should launch community education campaigns and offer rewards or certificates for active volunteers.
followUps.example: For example, universities can give extra training points or host fun weekend charity fairs on campus.
followUps.q: How can schools and organizations encourage more young people to volunteer?
followUps.reason: From a broader perspective, giving clear information and small rewards helps young people see volunteering as a gateway to self-discovery and self-development.

mindmapPoints.expand: This is because volunteers meet many different people and work together in groups, which helps them adjust and adapt to the social environment.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it is good for their social network and has a positive effect on their confidence.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Participating in volunteer work helps people improve their communication skills.

mindmapPoints.cue: Gaining practical experience and teamwork abilities
mindmapPoints.expand: For example, students who join a charity event learn how to plan tasks, talk with teammates, and solve real problems together.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is beneficial to people when they apply for future jobs.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Doing volunteer work helps young people gain practical experience and teamwork skills.

mindmapPoints.cue: Contributing positively to the local community
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because volunteers clean parks, teach poor children, or raise public awareness of environmental protection and healthy lifestyles.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has positive effects on both individuals and society.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Volunteering helps people make a contribution to their local community.
